identity.name: Monopotassium glutamate
identity.chemical_class: Potassium salt of L-glutamic acid (glutamate flavour-enhancer salt)

function.mechanism: Supplies free glutamate ions that enhance umami/savoury taste intensity.

adi.basis: Group ADI for glutamic acid (E620) and glutamates (E621-E625), expressed as glutamic acid.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found no genotoxicity concern but concluded that dietary exposure may exceed the group ADI in high consumers (and in toddlers/children at mean exposure in some scenarios).

fda.notes: Potassium glutamate and monopotassium glutamate are GRAS when used as flavour enhancers per 21 CFR 170.3(o)(11) and GMP.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group context for L-glutamic acid and its ammonium, calcium, monosodium and potassium salts).

concerns.summary: An in vitro human-lymphocyte study reported concentration-dependent chromosomal and DNA-damage signals for monopotassium glutamate, with statistical significance mainly at higher test concentrations.
A rat study with high MSG intake reported increased serum TMAO, reduced urinary TMAO excretion, and kidney-injury biomarker changes that improved after withdrawal.
A 2025 rat overconsumption study (0.8-3 g/kg/day) reported dose-related hepatic, renal, and cardiac toxicity markers associated with oxidative stress and inflammation.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation reported no genotoxicity concern for glutamic acid and glutamates (E620-E625).

A 2025 publication of GLP-style 28-day and 90-day rat dietary studies reported no toxicologically significant findings at tested doses (NOAEL up to approximately 3,170-3,620 mg/kg bw/day in the 90-day study).
A 2024 study reported no toxicity/genotoxicity at ADI-equivalent concentration in a Drosophila model.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported potential exceedance of the group ADI for glutamates in high consumers, and in some mean-intake scenarios for toddlers and children.

risk_assessment.rationale: E622 is approved/GRAS with established international evaluations, but EFSA identified plausible ADI exceedance in key subpopulations and recent experimental studies show mixed high-dose hazard signals; this supports a moderate-caution tier rather than limited or high.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day with exceedance concerns in high consumers
JECFA ADI not specified for glutamate-salt group
Mixed recent evidence: high-dose adverse findings vs GLP no-adverse-effect studies
No IARC classification and no major-jurisdiction ban identified
